text:
nina: heads-up — canary shows increased host-side CPU after kernel-selector roll last night, mostly on streaming tiny messages. noticed during heat-run.
ajay: saw same. p50 host_parse up ~1.6x, p99 decode CPU spike.
tom: link?
nina: https://grafana/reports/ingress/178001 1 main delta: host_parse_ns median 1.2ms -> 2.0ms.
olivia: tracing shows extra bytes-copies during `proto::unmarshal` when fragments cross iovecs. stack points to `memmove`/`copy` in decode path.
ajay: root cause: new chooser gives non-contig frame layout in some paths; host parse code currently coalesces by copying to contiguous buffer. copying on hot path kills tiny-message latency.
tom: options? revert chooser, or land a host zero-copy decoder that understands iovecs.
nina: ops wants a rollback to silence alerts. do that + a host fix PR.
ajay: I'll prototype `parse_view` — zero-copy proto view over iovec slices. heuristic: if total_len < 256 and iovec_count==1 -> fast path; else try multi-slice view; fallback to copy only if message spans >2 slices and isn't representable. Also noticed batcher sizes shrank because inter-token jitter increased.
olivia: interesting — what's the batcher threshold? we do size-first then time. jitter pushed it to emit earlier.
ajay: proposing a time-pref flag for streaming: if mean inter-arrival < 200us, accumulate up to time-window 1.5ms before emitting. that restores avg_batch_tokens for small-message flows.
tom: can we land both in one host patch and test in canary? ops prefers rollback first.
deploy-bot: deploy started service=ingress-canary tag=chooser-rollback-178001 commit=9f7a1de ETA ~90s :hourglass_flowing_sand:
ajay: quick local microbench results (docker replay):
```
baseline: parse_p50=1.2ms p95=2.7ms kvcache_hit=0.80 avg_batch=32
post-chooser: parse_p50=2.1ms p95=4.0ms kvcache_hit=0.77 avg_batch=13
host-patch (parse_view + time-pref): parse_p50=0.9ms p95=1.4ms kvcache_hit=0.82 avg_batch=30
```
olivia: nice kvcache uptick; maybe fewer temp allocations and less eviction churn. can you include flame and minimal repro in the PR?
ajay: yes, branch `perf/parse-view-178001` with bench, flame, unit test for fragmented iovecs.
tom: after PR, run 24h mixed-length replay, and watch kvcache eviction graph, p99 decode CPU, and batch size distribution. also run an ablation with old batcher to show difference.
nina: rollback complete and alerts quieted. once patch lands coordinate a canary with production-like smallwrite bursts. thanks all.
